<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Genesis 22:4">Targ. Y. ib. XXII, 4</cite> (ed. Amst. <cite ref="S00823"><he>קָטֵר</he></cite>, read: <cite ref="S00823"><he>קָטִר</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 22:15">Targ. Prov. XXII, 15</cite>; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 3:2:2">Koh. R. to III, 2</cite> [read:] <he>הן דאת קָטֵיר לולבך קְטֹר אלפך</he> when thou tiest thy Lulab, tie thy ship; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 6:5">Gen. R. s. 6</cite>, a. e., v. <cite ref="L00271"><he>לוּלָבָא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 9:10">Koh. R. to IX, 10</cite> <he>אייתון … וקַטְרוּ ברגלי</he> get a rope and tie it to my feet.

Y. Erub. X, 26ᶜ top קטיר בגמי (not קטר) tied with reed-grass. Y. Gitt. IV, 46ᵃ (we must not help captives to escape) מפני … דלא יהוון קַטְרִינוֹן this law is made for the benefit of the (remaining) captives, that they (the captors) may not chain them; a. fr.—2) (v. קָשַׁר) to gather, be covered.

<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Ezekiel 46:22">Targ. Ez. XLVI, 22</cite> <he>מְקַטְּרָן</he> fenced in (v. <cite ref="S00825">preced.</cite>).—Y. Ned. VI, 39ᵈ top <he>חלבא מקטרא</he> bound (curdled) milk, v. <cite ref="S00376"><he>קוֹם</he></cite>.
